# Re-entry Navigation Case Plan: Jarvier Xavier Frazier-Butler

**Participant Profile:** Jarvier Xavier Frazier-Butler | **Age:** 24 | **Supervision:** State Probation (Charleston County)  
**Housing:** Shield Ministries Cottage Housing (High Stability) | **LS/CMI Risk Level:** High (24/43)  
**Primary Clinical Target:** Antisocial Cognition & Workplace Stabilization  

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Dynamic Needs Assessment
Jarvier presents a **High Risk / High Needs** profile with strong motivation tied to family unification and stability. While his housing at Shield Ministries is currently highly stable, his primary dynamic risk factors include **Antisocial Cognition** (*Justifying* and *Cut-Off* thinking patterns), **Workplace Deficits** (0 payroll months in last 12), and **Authority Sensitivity** rooted in childhood family trauma. Static risk (juvenile record, past convictions) is noted but excluded from treatment targeting.

### Acute Triage Items (First 30 Days):
1. **Medication Continuity:** Secure uninterrupted supply of Remeron (mirtazapine) via Welvista / Fetter Health Care.
2. **Transportation Infrastructure:** Map CARTA bus routes for program attendance; initiate license restoration work.
3. **Legal Clarification:** Verify whether pending charges/warrants exist to preserve probation status.
4. **Program Fee Coordination:** Establish fee-deferral or transitional stipend plan for Shield Ministries fees.

---

## 2. Clinical & Facilitation Coaching Plan (Turn90 CBT Standards)

* **Modeling Neutrality (Standard 1.5):** When Jarvier displays rationalizations ('some crimes are justified'), staff must remain non-judgmental. Avoid debating ethics or morality. Utilize reflective inquiry: *"When you held that rule in the past, did it get you closer to being with your family or did it cost you your freedom?"*
* **Managing Frustration & Resistance (Standards 3.2 & 18.0):** Address his *Cut Off* pattern early. Frame all program expectations around his core self-interests: maintaining independence, providing for his kids, and avoiding probation sanctions.
* **Authority Sensitivity Trauma-Informed Approach:** Given his history of resisting arrest and emotional volatility with law enforcement, staff must maintain a predictable, collaborative, and non-confrontational coaching style. Reinforce his current positive relationship with his probation officer.

---

## 3. Measurable Action Goals

* **Goal 1 (Health & Stability):** Secure a 90-day refill of Remeron through Welvista by Week 2.
* **Goal 2 (Transit & Legal):** Attend an intake session with Father to Father Project for driver's license restoration and child support alignment by Week 3.
* **Goal 3 (Employment Placement):** Complete 2 interviews with fair-chance employers in demolition, landscape enhancement, or logistics by Week 4.
* **Goal 4 (CBT Mastery):** Complete Carey Guides modules on *Justifying* and *Problem-Solving* with 80%+ compliance by Week 4.

# My Fresh Start Action & Resource Guide: Jarvier Frazier-Butler

**Welcome to First Shift / Turn90 Re-entry Support!**  
Jarvier, this guide is built to support your vision: staying free, providing for your children and loved ones, and building a strong, lasting career in the Lowcountry. You have solid experience in construction cleanup, demolition, and cooking—and with stable housing at Shield Ministries, you are in a great position to take control of your future.

---

## 1. Local Community Resources For Your Fresh Start

### 🚌 Public Transit & Getting Around
* **CARTA Transit Passes & Route Mapping**  
  * **Services:** Fixed-route buses and workforce shuttle connections across Charleston and North Charleston.  
  * **Phone:** (843) 724-7420  
  * **Address:** Downtown / North Charleston Hubs  
  * **Link:** [Visit CARTA Website](https://ridecarta.com) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=Charleston+Area+Regional+Transportation+Authority)  
  * **Next Step:** Obtain your monthly CARTA pass at the transit hub and map your weekly bus route to First Shift and job interviews.

### ⚖️ Driver's License Restoration & Legal Support
* **Center for Fathering / Father to Father Project**  
  * **Services:** Assistance with driver's license restoration, child support modifications, and life coaching for dads.  
  * **Phone:** (843) 744-2126  
  * **Address:** 4925 Lacross Rd, North Charleston, SC 29406  
  * **Link:** [Visit Father to Father Website](https://scfathersandfamilies.com) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=4925+Lacross+Rd,+North+Charleston,+SC+29406)  
  * **Next Step:** Schedule an intake appointment to review your driver's license reinstatement path.

* **SC Legal Services - Charleston Office**  
  * **Services:** Free legal aid, court record clarification, and tenant rights support.  
  * **Phone:** (843) 720-7044  
  * **Address:** 2803 Carner Ave, North Charleston, SC 29405  
  * **Link:** [Visit SC Legal Website](https://sclegal.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=2803+Carner+Ave,+North+Charleston,+SC+29405)  
  * **Next Step:** Request a free background check review to clear up any questions regarding pending charges.

### 💊 Healthcare & Medication Assistance
* **Welvista Statewide Prescription Assistance**  
  * **Services:** Free 30/90-day delivery of maintenance prescription medications (including Remeron) for uninsured SC residents.  
  * **Phone:** (803) 933-9183  
  * **Link:** [Visit Welvista Website](https://welvista.org)  
  * **Next Step:** Fill out the online/paper application with your navigator to set up free mail delivery for your prescriptions.

* **Fetter Health Care Network**  
  * **Services:** Affordable primary care, dental, and behavioral health services on a sliding fee scale.  
  * **Phone:** (843) 722-4112  
  * **Address:** 51 Nassau St, Charleston, SC 29403  
  * **Link:** [Visit Fetter Health Website](https://fetterhealthcare.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=51+Nassau+St,+Charleston,+SC+29403)  
  * **Next Step:** Establish a local primary care doctor to manage health checkups and prescriptions.

---

## 2. Target Fair-Chance Job Matches

Here are vetted local employers offering competitive pay, steady shifts, and fair-chance opportunities that fit your background in physical work, cleanup, and site operations:

### 1. Lowcountry Framing & Carpentry Pros
* **Role:** Jobsite Laborer / Framing Apprentice  
* **Pay Rate:** $19.00 – $25.00 / hour  
* **Shift:** 6:30 AM – 3:00 PM (Monday – Friday, optional Saturday OT)  
* **Why It Fits:** Excellent match for your construction cleanup/demolition background. Fair-chance employer focusing on work ethic and daily punctuality. Provides tool reimbursement allowances.  
* **Apply Link:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=framing+carpentry&l=Charleston%2C+SC)

### 2. Palmetto Logistics & Distribution Hub
* **Role:** Order Selector / Warehouse Associate  
* **Pay Rate:** $18.00 – $22.50 / hour  
* **Shift:** Day Shift (6:30 AM – 3:00 PM)  
* **Why It Fits:** Active second-chance hiring policy with structured day shifts that fit public transit routes. Includes on-site OSHA forklift certification training.  
* **Apply Link:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=warehouse+logistics&l=Charleston%2C+SC)

### 3. Yardnique
* **Role:** Landscape Enhancement Crew Member  
* **Pay Rate:** Competitive Market Rate  
* **Shift:** Full-Time Year-Round Day Shift  
* **Location:** Ladson, SC  
* **Why It Fits:** Hands-on outdoor physical labor utilizing your stamina and outdoor work skills. Year-round employment stability.  
* **Apply Link:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.yardnique.com/careers/)

### 4. Brock Cabinets
* **Role:** Delivery Staff I  
* **Pay Rate:** $17.00 – $19.00 / hour  
* **Shift:** Day Shift  
* **Location:** North Charleston, SC  
* **Why It Fits:** Involves staging, loading, and delivering cabinet orders. Works out of North Charleston near public transit lines.  
* **Apply Link:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.brockcabinets.com/)

---

## 3. Your 4-Week Step-by-Step Action Checklist

### Week 1: Immediate Stabilization & Transit Setup
- [ ] Confirm daily medication setup through Welvista or Fetter Health Care.
- [ ] Obtain CARTA monthly transit pass and map daily bus travel times.
- [ ] Check in with state probation officer and share your First Shift schedule.

### Week 2: Legal Clarity & Skill Building
- [ ] Attend Father to Father Project intake for driver's license restoration.
- [ ] Complete legal check with SC Legal Services regarding open records.
- [ ] Complete CBT Carey Guide module on managing frustration and problem-solving.

### Week 3: Employment Applications & Resume Readiness
- [ ] Finalize resume with your Navigator highlighting cleanup, demolition, and general labor skills.
- [ ] Submit online applications to **Lowcountry Framing** and **Palmetto Logistics**.
- [ ] Practice mock interviews focusing on positive self-talk and professional communication.

### Week 4: Interviews & Career Placement
- [ ] Attend scheduled job interviews with fair-chance hiring partners.
- [ ] Establish a paycheck savings plan for program fees and family support.
- [ ] Celebrate 30-day program milestones with your First Shift support team!

Behavioral indicators represent how Jarvier's criminogenic risk factors manifest in daily life. Understanding these patterns prepares
staff to anticipate friction points and select coaching interventions.
Behavioral Component Observed Manifestation & Thinking Patterns
Typical Triggers Transportation failures, structural instability (eviction history), unemployment, and perceived disrespect
or challenging situations from authority figures.
Escalation Tendencies Recurrent physical violence and aggressive resistance. When facing legal or community supervision
pressure, he has historically escalated to physical fights and resisting arrest.
Thinking Pattern: JUSTIFYING Neutralizes criminal guilt. Specifically states: 'the bad ones I do feel some kind of remorse, but some of
them I feel are justified.' This allows him to bypass prosocial morals when facing crises.
Thinking Pattern: CUT OFF A tendency to give up or walk away from responsibilities when things become highly frustrating or when
structural barriers (like transportation) seem insurmountable.
Authority Response Style Highly sensitive and defensive. Has a documented record of assaulting and fighting police officers
serving process, though currently reports a highly cooperative stance with his PO.

3. PATTERN OVER TIME
Delinquency Trajectory: Jarvier's justice involvement began exceptionally early, with a first arrest at age 10. His history contains
a dense juvenile record which he is unable to fully recall, followed by a severe escalation in adulthood. He has been incarcerated
upon conviction, recently completing a two-year prison term under a DOC sentence (Burglary 2nd/Assault 1st).
Community Supervision Violations: His community supervision history is marked by instability. He has had his probation and
parole suspended/revoked, and was arrested on supervision for public intoxication, malicious property damage, and pedestrian in
the roadway, which co-occurred with an armed robbery the same night. This trajectory highlights a pattern of rapid escalation from
minor property offenses to severe physical violence.
4. ACUTE / EMERGENCY NEEDS
These immediate stabilization needs must be addressed during his first 30 days to facilitate program compliance:
• Transportation Stabilization: His driver's license is suspended. He currently relies on walking or unreliable public transit. He
needs immediate scheduling support, bus passes, and route mapping to attend Shield Ministries' programs regularly.
• Medication Compliance: He takes Remron (mirtazapine) daily. Reentry staff must verify he has an uninterrupted supply of his
medication and access to medical providers.
• Financial/Program Fee Debt: He has immediate obligations to pay program fees to Shield Ministries. Lacking a payroll job, he
requires rapid transitional employment or fee-deferral options to prevent financial crisis.
5. STRUCTURAL STABILITY FACTORS
• Housing Stability: High stability. He is currently residing in 'college' or Shield Ministries cottage housing and expresses immense
satisfaction ('I love it'). This safe, structured environment is a major protective factor.
• Education: Highly stable. Holds a GED and has completed 12th grade, leaving him well-prepared for vocational training without
academic remedial barriers.
• Employment History: Unstable but skilled. Possesses experience in construction cleanup, demolition cleanup, and cooking.
Jobs typically ended due to a lack of reliable transportation. He holds a strong desire to work.
• Substance Use: Historically used alcohol which contributed to his severe arrest on active supervision. He has been sober during
incarceration, but needs relapse prevention as his work and social circles expand.
6. LEGAL & PLACEMENT CONSTRAINTS
• Supervision Schedule: Subject to active state probation. Requires coordination of program times with probation officer visits
(whom he reports is fair and reasonable).
• Pending Charges: He reports 'I might have pending charges, I don't know.' Staff must conduct immediate legal advocacy and a
records check to clarify any unresolved warrants or pending court dates.
• Placement Safety: No Sex Offender Registry requirements. However, his history of severe physical violence and resisting arrest
requires careful monitoring in group environments to manage anger/conflict triggers.
7. RESPONSIVITY & ENGAGEMENT PROFILE
• Coaching Style: Supportive & Cognitive-Behavioral: Jarvier is highly motivated to work and lead a law-abiding life, and he
deeply loves his family (wife/girlfriend and children). Staff should leverage this family motivation in case planning. Use
non-confrontational CBT (e.g., MRT or Carey Guides) to address his Justifying and Cut Off thinking patterns.
• Trauma-Informed Approach: He has a severe history of childhood family abuse, neglect, and removal from the home by DSS.
This trauma likely drives his authority sensitivity and emotional reactivity. Staff must maintain a calm, predictable, and supportive
demeanor.
• Authority Figure Sensitivity: Due to his history of resisting and assaulting police officers, aggressive or overly confrontational
supervision will trigger a defensive, defiant response. Reentry coaches should emphasize collaboration and problem-solving,
